comments.text:
"The story of this island was never about being clever, it was just luck. It was about standing on the right ground at the right time in history, it was about luck, not genius" How historically illiterate can a person get? 

Wealth is created by productive labour, not just by having minerals or oil in the Earth or free flowing rivers (Adam Smith 101).

Britain produced the best inventors, engineers and scientists and it was their genius that underpinned the industrial revolution. The industrial revolution that started in England and spread to the rest of the world to produce the modern world we see today.

From James Watt who revolutionised steam engines to do useful work, freeing industry from dependence on raw muscle power of men and animals (the world literally names the unit of power after him i.e. the Watt), to George Stephenson and Richard Trevithick who pioneered the steam locomotive, inventing the steam trains that were needed to move mined coal, iron ore, timbre and later on, people to the steelworks and factories, then moving the finished manufactured goods to where they were needed, (often the docks for export).

World remouned engineers like Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed the metal bridges and tunnels for our railways. Genius scientists like Sir Isaac Newton, whose laws of motion and mechanics provided the scientific knowledge for the technology of the industrial revolution. 

Improvements to communications were also essential to the rapid growth of industry. The telephone, invented by a Scotsman, Sir Alexander Graham Bell, was a big improvement over the telegraph, by which people could already communicate instantly with the rest of the world - and this was in the Victorian age!(the telegraph also being a British invention btw).

The machines in the factories that helped turn raw materials into finished goods for local sale or trade like the Spinning Jenny, the power loom and the cotton gin were all invented by Brits.
The Bessemer process (the first method for economically mass producing steel) was invented by Henry Bessemer in London, stainless steel was invented in Sheffield by Harry Brearly...and many more essential inventions.

The success of Britain was down to the success of the Brits themselves. If it was all down to what natural resources you had then Africa would be the richest continent on Earth.

But perhaps our greatest failure has been cultural. World remouned engineers like Isambard Kingdom Brunel designed the metal bridges and tunnels for our railways. Genius scientists like Sir Isaac Newton, whose laws of motion and mechanics provided the scientific knowledge for the technology of the industrial revolution. 

Improvements to communications were also essential to the rapid growth of industry. The telephone, invented by a Scotsman, Sir Alexander Graham Bell, was a big improvement over the telegraph, by which people could already communicate instantly with the rest of the world - and this was in the Victorian age!(the telegraph also being a British invention btw).

comments.text:
Estimates suggest the UK government missed out on hundreds of billions in potential revenue by privatizing oil and gas, with one analysis indicating a loss of up to £400 billion compared to Norway's state-led approach. Instead of generating state wealth, privatized companies paid £70.7bn in dividends between 2010 and 2025, rather than reinvesting in lower energy costs. 

Sources: National Resource Government Institute - Did the U.K. Miss Out on £400 Billion Worth of Oil Revenue?
Blog post 5 October 2015 David Manley Keith Myer

Quatr - Norway's Sovereign Wealth Fund: Creating Lasting Prosperity 21 Nov 2025

BBC - Has the UK squandered its North Sea riches?
Published
8 October 2012

National Scot - North Sea oil 'lost opportunity' cost UK £500 billion wealth fund
5th April 2018

Aberdeen & Grampian Chamber of Commerce - North Sea tax receipts plummet as windfall tax hits investment
Chamber News August 14, 2025

The Conservation - Would more North Sea drilling lower UK energy bills? Our analysis says no
Published: March 17, 2026

While Norway accumulated massive public wealth through state ownership, the UK focused on privatisation, resulting in lower long-term tax receipts.

Had the UK maintained public ownership, it could have potentially avoided roughly £70 billion in energy costs between 2022 and 2030, according to projections regarding net-zero pathways.

Shareholders of privatized energy companies took at least £70.7 billion in dividends between 2010 and 2025.

The UK government earned only around £1.2 billion (in 1980s prices) from the initial oil company privatisations, a figure that is widely seen as failing to reflect the long-term value of the assets.

Government revenue from oil and gas was £9 billion in 2022–23 and dropped to £4.5 billion in 2024–25.
